h1: The open source vector database: free, self-hosted, Apache 2.0
sub: Milvus is a free, Apache 2.0 open source vector database from the LF AI & Data Foundation, written in Go and C++ for high-performance search at scale. Start with pip install, grow to tens of billions of vectors on Kubernetes, and keep the same API.
proof: Scales to tens of billions of vectors

benefits.title: Open source, for real
benefits.body: Apache 2.0 and governed by the LF AI & Data Foundation. Hundreds of contributors build it in the open on GitHub.

benefits.title: Fast on every CPU
benefits.body: The Knowhere engine picks SSE, AVX2, AVX512 or ARM instructions at runtime, and GPU indexes such as CAGRA run on NVIDIA hardware.

benefits.title: Scales out, not up
benefits.body: Storage and compute are separated. Stateless query, streaming and data nodes scale independently on Kubernetes to tens of billions of vectors.

benefits.title: Trusted in production
benefits.body: NVIDIA, Salesforce, Walmart, eBay, IBM and Reddit are on the Milvus adopter wall; Meituan runs 10B+ vectors on self-hosted Milvus.

feature_blocks.title: Deploy a self-hosted vector database: pip, Docker, Kubernetes or managed
feature_blocks.body: Same engine and API at every size, sized per the install overview. Distributed Milvus installs with the official Helm chart or Milvus Operator.
bullets: Milvus Lite: pip install, a local file, up to a few million vectors for notebooks and prototypes
Standalone: one Docker Compose file (milvus-standalone, etcd, MinIO), up to 100M vectors
Distributed on Kubernetes: 100M to tens of billions of vectors, tiered storage, 65,536 collections by default, partition keys for millions of tenants

code.h2: Local vector database in Python: pip install to first search
code.intro: Milvus Lite ships with pymilvus. No server, no Docker, no account: the database is a local file.
code.code:
# pip install -U "pymilvus[milvus-lite]"
import random
from pymilvus import MilvusClient

client = MilvusClient("milvus_demo.db")  # Milvus Lite: data lives in this local file
client.create_collection(collection_name="demo", dimension=768)

docs = ["Milvus is an open-source vector database.", "It runs on a laptop or on Kubernetes."]
vecs = [[random.random() for _ in range(768)] for _ in docs]  # swap in your embedding model
client.insert(collection_name="demo",
              data=[{"id": i, "vector": v, "text": t} for i, (v, t) in enumerate(zip(vecs, docs))])

print(client.search(collection_name="demo", data=[vecs[0]], limit=2, output_fields=["text"]))
code.note: To move to a server, pass its URI (for example http://localhost:19530) to MilvusClient.

faqs: Are open source vector databases free for commercial use?

Milvus is: Apache 2.0 permits commercial use, modification and redistribution at no cost, and released code stays Apache 2.0. Milvus is a graduated LF AI & Data Foundation project; Zilliz is its major contributor. You pay only for the infrastructure you run.
What is the best open source vector database for RAG?

Pick by workload. Milvus fits RAG that needs hybrid search, filtering and scale: built-in BM25, partition keys for per-tenant retrieval, and LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations, from a laptop file to a Kubernetes cluster.
Open source vs managed vector database: which should you choose?

Self-hosting Milvus gives full control of data and infrastructure cost; your team runs upgrades, scaling and backups. Zilliz Cloud runs the same engine behind the same MilvusClient API, so moving either way needs no rewrite.
How much RAM does a self-hosted vector database need?

Raw float32 vectors take dimensions × 4 bytes each before index overhead. Milvus cuts that with SQ8 (75% less than FP32), IVF_RABITQ (1-to-32 compression) or DiskANN on NVMe; estimate with milvus.io/tools/sizing.
Is a self-hosted, on-premise vector database production-ready at scale?
Yes. Distributed Milvus runs on Kubernetes with replicas and independent scaling. Meituan runs 10B+ vectors on self-hosted Milvus; Read AI serves 20–50 ms retrieval to millions of users.

final.h2: Run an open source vector database in five minutes
final.body: pip install pymilvus, open a local file, and search. Move to Standalone or Kubernetes as data grows, or hand operations to Zilliz Cloud, with no rewrite.
